newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat jumps amid late new crop flurry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat jumps amid late new crop flurry.

text.p: LIFFE grains firmed, with a late flurry of activity on the new crop ahead of the holiday.
Traders said there was more shipper activity as buyers attempted to set prices in what looks like an increasingly tight UK market.

"I think it's mainly on sentiment," one physical market trader said. "There's no selling going on from farms. There's been a bit of consumer enquiry. And there's been a bit of forceful shipper buying. It's pushed people into the futures."

A firm international market helped, he said. He felt the rise on November was overdone and questioned whether buyers had really needed to pay two sterling higher. "They scrambled over each other," he said.
An easier sterling could have been expected to trigger a rise, but the market gathered more momentum than justified by currencies.
November was the most active month on wheat, with 311 lots of a total 633. It last traded 2.00 stg higher at 99.25 stg.
July was next most active, with 130 lots. It last traded 1.15 stg up at 103.90.
November also dominated barley, with 46 of a total 51 lots. It last traded 1.50 stg up at 96.25.
The LIFFE wheat and barley markets are now closed for the holiday. They re-open on Tuesday, April 1.
